style.notes: KJV-MWB keeps the KJV’s own vocabulary and archaic forms (thou, thee, thy, thine, shall). Name insertions add only the name and punctuation.

rules.sourceText: My son, hear the instruction of thy father, and forsake not the law of thy mother:
grammaticalConditions: The name follows the existing vocative "My son" and is set off by commas.
"My son" is kept exactly as written; it is never changed for any reader.
riskReasons: Names the reader’s own father and mother as the source of instruction.
rules.reviewQuestion: Verse 8 refers to the instruction of "thy father" and "thy mother". With the reader’s name added, it speaks of the reader’s own parents. Is personal address pastorally appropriate here, including for readers whose parents did not teach them in faith?

riskReasons: Historical proposal that replaced KJV wording.
rules.rejectionReason: Replaces KJV vocabulary ("an end", "thine expectation", "shall") with another translation’s wording ("a future for you", "your hope", "will"). Fails versional integrity for KJV-MWB.
rules.notes: Kept for the record so this wording is never silently reused. Superseded by kjv-mwb.PRO.23.18.b.

reviews.reviewerRole: Product decision on version integrity (not a theological approval)
reviews.rejectionReason: Source wording mismatch with the KJV.

rules.sourceText: For surely there is an end; and thine expectation shall not be cut off.
grammaticalConditions: The name is a vocative set off by commas between "and" and "thine expectation".
All KJV wording ("For surely", "there is an end", "thine expectation", "shall not be cut off") is kept.
riskReasons: The assurance in verse 18 rests on the exhortation in verse 17.
rules.reviewQuestion: Verse 18’s assurance follows verse 17 ("be thou in the fear of the LORD all the day long"). Should the name appear in verse 18 when it is shown on its own (daily verse, share card), or only when verse 17 is shown with it?
rules.notes: KJV-faithful candidate replacing the rejected kjv-mwb.PRO.23.18.a.

rules.sourceText: Fear thou not; for I am with thee: be not dismayed; for I am thy God: I will strengthen thee; yea, I will help thee; yea, I will uphold thee with the right hand of my righteousness.
grammaticalConditions: The name is a vocative after "Fear thou not", before the existing semicolon.
riskReasons: Direct divine speech.
Addressed to Israel collectively as God’s servant.
rules.reviewQuestion: This is God’s direct speech to Israel as His servant (Isaiah 41:8–9). May a personal name be inserted into divine speech addressed to Israel, or should this verse stay unpersonalised in KJV-MWB?

rules.sourceText: Beloved, I wish above all things that thou mayest prosper and be in health, even as thy soul prospereth.
grammaticalConditions: The name follows the existing address "Beloved," and is set off by commas.
riskReasons: Letter addressed to a specific person, Gaius.
rules.reviewQuestion: John’s wish is addressed to Gaius (3 John 1:1). Is it appropriate to address a personal wish written to a specific person to the reader by name?

rules.sourceText: Now the God of hope fill you with all joy and peace in believing, that ye may abound in hope, through the power of the Holy Ghost.
rules.author: Paul
rules.speaker: The apostle Paul
rules.audience: The believers in Rome, in benediction (collective)
grammaticalConditions: Founder reference wording from the Stage D.1 brief, recorded exactly so it can be reviewed.
riskReasons: Collective benediction to the church in Rome.
Replaces the plural pronoun “you” with one person while “ye may abound” remains.
rules.reviewQuestion: Founder reference (Mode A): “Now the God of hope fill [Name] with all joy… that ye may abound in hope…”. The plural “you” becomes one person while “ye” remains, and a benediction to a church becomes an individual one. Should this verse be personalised in the text at all?
rules.notes: Expected to fail automated validation (pronounReplaced, residualPronoun). Kept so reviewers see the founder example and why it is held back.
